title: Diff Review Dojo — Code Review Trainer
description: Twelve short fictional pull requests in JS, TS, TSX, SQL and CSS, each hiding one real bug — an off-by-one loop, an async forEach, SQL built by string interpolation, a stale-response race, a boolean comparator, a clickable div, a UTC date key, a BETWEEN on timestamps, a removed focus ring, rounding money, a mutating reducer and a deleted null guard. Click the guilty line, pick a bug category, and the reveal explains the bug and shows the fix, with score, streak, and unified or split views.
prompt: Build 'Diff Review Dojo', a code-review trainer. Write about ten short fictional diffs in JS, TS, SQL and CSS, each hiding exactly one real bug — off-by-one, missing await, SQL injection via string concatenation, a race condition, a wrong comparator, an accessibility regression, a timezone bug and so on. Let me click a line to leave a review comment with a bug category, then submit or approve; the reveal should explain the bug and show the fix. Keep score and a streak. Offer unified and split diff views with realistic syntax colouring — write the highlighter yourself. Every bug must be genuinely wrong, not a matter of taste. Give it a calm dojo feel: washi paper, sumi ink, one vermilion seal.

methodology: Scoring rules as a decision table: right line + right category = 10, right line + wrong category = 5, wrong line = 0 with the correct line named, approve = 0; each branch has an explicit test and streak/best are checked after each.
Answer-key run: a full playthrough driven by the window.__dojo hook proves every one of the twelve bugs is gradable as a clean hit and that the maximum is exactly 120.
Content review of each diff by hand: every planted bug was checked to be objectively wrong (e.g. $100 / 3 rounds to 99.99, toISOString is UTC, BETWEEN '2026-03-31' stops at midnight).
View parity: split view pairs removed and added runs row by row, keeps the same line test ids, and grading and bug highlighting work there too.
Tokenizer checks per language: keywords and comments get the right token classes in TS and SQL, and a multi-line template literal keeps string colouring across lines.
Keyboard path: line-number buttons open the composer with Enter; validation, edit with the saved category preselected, and delete.
risks: Hunk line-number arithmetic: an off-by-one in the viewer itself would point the reveal at the wrong line.
The regex highlighter must never inject raw code as HTML — code containing '<' (TSX) is escaped before tokens are wrapped.
Empty alternation groups in a tokenizer regex match everywhere and silently disable later token rules (caught during build for SQL and CSS).
Split view renders two cells per context line, so test ids must stay unique.
qa.playwright: Everything is DOM, so role and test-id locators do the work; each diff line row carries data-testid line-N keyed to its index in the diff, identical in unified and split views. The hard part is scale — twelve rounds — which the answer-key test handles by reading the current diff's bug line and category from a small window.__dojo hook rather than hard-coding twelve answers, with an explicit test.setTimeout for the long run. The submit button is truly disabled until a comment exists, so the spec can assert toBeDisabled() rather than inspecting styles. ?seed= shuffles the order with a seeded PRNG, and the spec checks it is a stable permutation.
coverage: Clean hit: score, streak, bug highlight, explanation, fix, focus to Next
Half credit, miss with the correct line named, approve on a buggy diff
Composer validation, keyboard open, edit with preselected category, delete
Split view pairing and SQL syntax tokens; grading in split view
Full perfect run to 120 and best-streak persistence
Seeded shuffle is a deterministic permutation

a11y: Each line number is a real button with a name like “Comment on added line 15”, the composer uses a labelled radio group for categories and moves focus into it, and verdicts and score changes are announced through live regions. Diff colour is always paired with +/− signs, and bug highlights add a thick edge marker as well as colour.
